newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India down on results, oil prices.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India down on results, oil prices.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) closed marginally lower on Wednesday after a recent series of disappointing company results and concerns over a hike in petroleum prices unsettled the market.
"The market's movement today was a combination of poor first half results and worries over a petroleum price increase that seems imminent," a trader said.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed down 1.42 points, or 2.24 percent, at 61.89 points, with the premium over the local market at 17.66 percent compared with Tuesday's 17.28 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index tumbled 76.22 points, or 2.43 percent, closing provisionally at 3,063.11.
"Local markets saw speculative selling, which affected the GDR market, because it's been looking for India to consolidate and go further," a dealer said.
"Speculators have the market and they want to drive it down over the next two days so they can buy it back lower, and they're selling into a fairly thin market," he added.
Traders said that Century Textiles, which posted poor first half earnings earlier this week, had affected the market.
There are a lot of exposed positions out there," said one.
Century closed down at $45.00/$50.00, down 50 cents from Tuesday and even further from Monday's $6.00 fall to 58.00/$73.00, when it reported a 67 percent fall in net profit.
The GDR had been trading at $75 eight days ago.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended up 0.70 points, or 1.04 percent, at 68.28 points, a premium of 30.72 percent over the local market, compared with yesterday's 29.77 percent.
The Korea Composite Index closed down 2.91 points at 744.14.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended up 0.88 points, or 0.97 percent, at 91.60, a premium of 4.28 percent after 1.84 percent yesterday.
The Taiwan Weighted Index finished up 41.48 points or 0.62 percent, at 6,729.36 points.
